Rashi on Nedarim 61b:1:1.english: Is that to say that Rabbi Meir, etc. - As I explained.

Rashi on Nedarim 61b:1:2.hebrew: לספיקא - דכיון דאיכא לספוקי אי משמע עד שיצא או עד שיגיע, ודאי בדליכא ספיקא הרהר בדעתו בשעת הנדר, דהיינו עד שיגיע. ורבי יוסי אומר עד שיצא, דסבר מעייל איניש נפשיה לספיקא, דאיכא לספוקי שמא עד שיצא קאמר:
Rashi on Nedarim 61b:1:2.english: [Into] uncertainty - For since there is room for doubt whether [his wording] implies "until [Passover] ends" or "until it arrives," he certainly had in mind at the time of the vow [the meaning] in which there is no doubt, which is "until it arrives." And Rabbi Yosei says "until it ends" — for he holds [that] a person places himself into uncertainty, since there is room for doubt [that] perhaps he meant "until it ends."

Rashi on Nedarim 61b:2:1.hebrew: שתי כיתי בנות - משתי נשים שנשא זו אחר זו, וכל אחת ילדה שתי בנות:
Rashi on Nedarim 61b:2:1.english: Two groups of daughters - From two women whom he married one after the other, and each one gave birth to two daughters.

Rashi on Nedarim 61b:2:2.hebrew: כולן אסורות חוץ וכו' דברי רבי מאיר - דקסבר רבי מאיר מעייל איניש לספיקא, דלא איזדהר הארוס בשעת קידושין דלא ליתי לידי קלקול. והואיל דלא ידעינן הי מינייהו קידש, כולן אסורות:
Rashi on Nedarim 61b:2:2.english: All of them are prohibited apart from, etc., [this is] the statement of Rabbi Meir - For Rabbi Meir holds [that] a person brings [himself] into uncertainty, as the betrother was not careful at the time of betrothal so that he would not come to a mishap. And since we do not know which of them he betrothed, all of them are prohibited.

Rashi on Nedarim 61b:2:3.english: Except for the younger [daughter] of the younger [group] - For according to all [opinions], she does not have the designation "older."

Rashi on Nedarim 61b:3:1.english: Rabbi Yosei says: They are all permitted, etc. - For he holds [that] a person does not bring himself into uncertainty.

Rashi on Nedarim 61b:4:1.hebrew: מוחלפת השיטה - כלומר, אפיך מתניתין דנדרים ואימא: לרבי מאיר, מעייל איניש כו':
Rashi on Nedarim 61b:4:1.english: The opinion is reversed - That is to say, reverse the Mishnah of Nedarim and say: According to Rabbi Meir, a person brings [himself into a doubtful situation], etc.

Rashi on Nedarim 61b:4:2.english: And it is taught - [It is said] in a declarative tone, [proving] that [the attribution of the opinions] is reversed.

Rashi on Nedarim 61b:4:3.english: This is the principle: anything whose time is fixed - Such as festivals.

Rashi on Nedarim 61b:4:4.english: Until it ends - For he holds that a person brings himself into [a state of] doubt.

Rashi on Nedarim 61b:5:1.english: [If] one said, "Konam that I will not taste wine until the vintage [batzir]" - [The harvest] of grapes.

Rashi on Nedarim 61b:5:2.english: Until the olive harvest - The picking of olives.

Rashi on Nedarim 61b:5:3.hebrew: וכל שאין זמנו קבוע - כגון קציר ובציר, דזמנין הוו בחריפי וזמנין הוו באפלי:
Rashi on Nedarim 61b:5:3.english: And any [occasion] whose time is not fixed - Such as the grain harvest and the grape harvest, which sometimes occur early and sometimes occur late.

Rashi on Nedarim 61b:6:1.hebrew: עד הקיץ - עד שעת לקיטת תאנים, או שאמר עד שיהא הקיץ — שניהם משמע דאינו אסור אלא עד שיתחיל העם להכניס תאנים בכלכלות, וזהו בתחילת הקיץ:
Rashi on Nedarim 61b:6:1.english: Until the summer - [meaning] until the time of gathering figs, or if he said "until it will be summer" — both imply that he is only prohibited until the people begin to bring in figs in baskets, and this is at the beginning of the summer.

Rashi on Nedarim 61b:6:2.hebrew: אמר עד שיעבור הקיץ אסור עד שיוכפלו המקצועות - עד שמכפילין הסכינים שקצצו בהן התאנים ומצניעין אותן, כמו מקפלין את הכלים (שבת דף קיג.). ענין אחר: שיקפלו — עד שחורץ אותן בקופיץ ועושין אותן שירטי"ט, כמו ליטרא קציעות, ולשון יכפילו על שם שמניחין זו על זו. ותרוייהו — שיעבור ויקפילו — משמע בסוף הקיץ:
Rashi on Nedarim 61b:6:2.english: [If] he said: "Until the summer has passed," he is forbidden until the maktzuot are folded [yukhpelu] - [That is,] until they fold away the knives with which they cut the figs and store them away, like "folding garments" (Shabbat 113a). Another explanation: "that they fold [sheyakpilu]" — until one scores them with a cleaver and makes them into shirtit [pressed cakes], like a litra of dried figs; and the term "they double" [yakhpilu] is used because they place one [fig] on top of another. And both of them — "has passed" and "they fold" — imply [the time] at the end of the summer.

Rashi on Nedarim 61b:7:1.hebrew: ולא כלכלה של ענבים - משמע, אף על פי שהבציר הוי סמוך לאלתר לקיץ, לא אמרינן שזה נתכוון לכלכלה של ענבים, אלא ודאי אינו אסור אלא עד תאנים:
Rashi on Nedarim 61b:7:1.english: And not a basket of grapes - This implies [that] even though the grape harvest is immediately after the summer [fig season], we do not say that this [vower] intended a basket of grapes; rather, he is certainly prohibited only until [the harvest of] figs.

Rashi on Nedarim 61b:7:2.hebrew: עגבים בכלל תאנים - ואסור עד כלכלה של ענבים: ענבים לא מקצצו ביד אלא בסכין, ולא דמו כלל לתאנים, הלכך לא הוו בכלל תאנים:
Rashi on Nedarim 61b:7:2.english: Grapes are included with figs - And he is forbidden until [the gathering of] a basket of grapes. [According to the first Tanna, however,] grapes are not plucked by hand, rather [cut] with a knife, and are not similar at all to figs; therefore, they are not included with figs.

Rashi on Nedarim 61b:8:1.hebrew: ענבים נמי כי מירדדן - כשמתבשלין יפה יפה שנושרין ענבים מן האשכול, מקצצו נמי בידא כתאנים. הלכך, הוו בכלל תאנים:
Rashi on Nedarim 61b:8:1.english: Grapes, too, when they are ripe [ki miraddedan] - When they ripen very well, such that grapes drop from the cluster, they are also plucked by hand like figs. Therefore, they are included in [the category of] figs.

Rashi on Nedarim 61b:9:1.english: It was taught: Most of the maktzu'ot were folded up - [That is,] those figs that remained in the fields and on the trees.

Tosafot on Nedarim 61b:2:1.hebrew: ורמינהו מי שיש לו שתי כיתי בנות משתי נשים - מכל אשה שתי בנות, קטנה וגדולה. משנה היא בקידושין פרק האומר (דף סד:), דסבר רבי מאיר דמחית אינש נפשיה לספיקא, ושמא קרי לה לגדולה קטנה שבגדולות; ורבי יוסי אמר וכו', דלא מעייל אינש נפשיה לספיקא, וגדולה דקאמר — גדולה ממש:
Tosafot on Nedarim 61b:2:1.english: And [the Gemara] raises a contradiction: "One who has two groups of daughters from two wives" - From each wife, two daughters — a younger one and an older one. It is a Mishnah in Kiddushin, chapter HaOmer (64b), where Rabbi Meir holds that a person places himself into uncertainty, and perhaps he calls the younger [daughter] of the older [group] "older"; whereas Rabbi Yosei says, etc., that a person does not bring himself into uncertainty, and "older" that he says [means] literally the oldest:

Tosafot on Nedarim 61b:4:1.hebrew: מוחלפת השיטה - ואיפוך מתני': דר"מ לדרבי יוסי, ודרבי יוסי לדר"מ:
Tosafot on Nedarim 61b:4:1.english: The attribution of the opinions is reversed - And reverse [the opinions in] the Mishnah: [attribute that of] Rabbi Meir to Rabbi Yosei, and [that of] Rabbi Yosei to Rabbi Meir.

Tosafot on Nedarim 61b:4:2.hebrew: והתניא - בניחותא. ולמאי דמסיק התם אביי, בלישנא פליגי, ואין צריך לומר "מוחלפת השיטה":
Tosafot on Nedarim 61b:4:2.english: And it is taught [in a baraita] - [This is read] as a declarative statement. And according to what Abaye concludes there, they disagree regarding the wording, and there is no need to say, "The [attribution of the] opinions is reversed."

Tosafot on Nedarim 61b:5:1.hebrew: עד הבציר אינו אסור אלא עד שיגיע - וה"ה נמי אם אמר עד שיהא, כיון דאין זמנו קבוע, כדמפרש ואזיל:
Tosafot on Nedarim 61b:5:1.english: "Until the grape harvest, it is forbidden only until it arrives" - And the same applies as well if he said "until it will be," since its time is not fixed, as [the Mishnah] goes on to explain.

Tosafot on Nedarim 61b:5:2.hebrew: זה הכלל כל שזמנו קבוע כו' - כמו בציר; אמר "עד שיהא", אינו אסור אלא עד שיגיע לבד. בפ"ג בקידושין (דף סד:) י"מ דקציר ובציר הוי זמנו קבוע, ואין זמנו [קבוע] כגון דאמר "עד שילך פלוני למקום פלוני", שאינו יודע כמה יאחר. ול"נ, דהא אמר: "עד שיהא הקיץ — עד שיתחילו לתת בכלכלות", אלמא אינו אסור עד שיצא, ואין זמנו קבוע תפסינן ליה:
Tosafot on Nedarim 61b:5:2.english: This is the principle: any [occasion] whose time is fixed, etc. - [And that whose time is not fixed is] like grape harvest: [if] he said, "until it will be," it is forbidden only until it arrives. In the third chapter of Kiddushin (64b), there are some who explain that grain harvest and grape harvest are [considered cases whose] time is fixed, and [a case whose] time is not [fixed] is, for example, where he said, "until So-and-so goes to such-and-such a place," for he does not know how long he will delay. And it does not appear [correct] to me, for behold it says [in the Mishnah]: "Until the summer [fig harvest] — until they begin to put [figs] in baskets"; thus [we see that] it is not forbidden until it ends, and we treat it as [an occasion whose] time is not fixed.

Tosafot on Nedarim 61b:6:1.english: Kayitz [summer] - [It is so called] because they cut [kotztzim] the figs. [The harvest] of figs is called kayitz because it is cut by hand, whereas grapes, which are cut with a knife, are called betzirah [vintage].

Tosafot on Nedarim 61b:8:1.hebrew: ענבים נמי כי מירדדן - פירוש: כשנתייבשו, נקצצות ביד. [ל"א] מיזרדן, כמו חבילי זרדין:
Tosafot on Nedarim 61b:8:1.english: "Grapes, too, when [they] mirdaddan" - Explanation: When they have dried out, they are plucked by hand. [Another reading:] mizeraddan, like "bundles of shoots" [chavilei zeradin].

Tosafot on Nedarim 61b:9:1.hebrew: עד שיקפלו רוב המקצועות - סכינים שקוצצין בהם עיגולי תאנים, והעיגולים עצמן נקראין קציעות:
Tosafot on Nedarim 61b:9:1.english: Until most of the maktzu'ot are folded away - [Maktzu'ot are] knives with which they cut fig cakes, and the cakes themselves are called ketzi'ot.
